They argue that 'handmade' or 'homemade' is not inherently safe or good, because producers may lack awareness of right and wrong. Using farmers as an example, they describe how growers are told to use certain chemical sprays to make vegetables and fruit look better and sell at higher prices, and they comply. The quoted post provides additional context, warning readers not to trust extremely low-priced oils claiming to be pure cold-pressed, urging verification of brand credentials and certifications, noting raw material costs exceed finished product prices, and stating that handmade labeling is not a quality guarantee.
